vBRIEFInfo.description: Plan for PAN-2145: Thin routes/conversations.ts (5306 lines) behind src/lib/overdeck/ door modules (two-door route-thinning, Approach A)

plan.title: Decompose src/dashboard/server/routes/conversations.ts into focused door modules (two-door thinning)
plan.author: agent:claude-opus-4-8

narratives.Problem: src/dashboard/server/routes/conversations.ts is 5306 lines (baselined at 5306 in scripts/file-size-baseline.txt; the #1 server god file, +418 since the issue was filed). It holds 2667 lines of domain helpers (session spawning, runtime readiness, delivery/control-channel, message transforms, fork pipeline, archived-list, control acks) BEFORE the first of 34 HttpRouter.add registrations. The server BOOT path even imports from it (src/dashboard/server/main.ts imports recoverStuckForks + waitForInFlightForkPipelines). Every conversation-lifecycle change lands in this one file. It is pipeline hot-path machinery (agent spawn / live-control / forks).
narratives.Proposal: Approach A (two-door route-thinning), the campaign-level ruling of 2026-07-02 confirmed by the operator; the issue body's barrel-split ask is superseded (a route-file barrel split just relocates the god file — the workspaces barrel split produced merge-ops.ts at 1925 lines). Keep all 34 routes and conversationsRouteLayer in routes/conversations.ts, but move each handler's domain logic into NEW sibling door modules under src/lib/overdeck/ (conversation-diffs, -archive, -reads, -delivery [+ -message if it would exceed 1000], -runtime, -forks), rewriting each handler as a thin adapter (parse -> one door call -> jsonResponse, <=~40 lines). Repoint every importer of a moved symbol in the same commit (no re-export shims); this also fixes the boot-imports-a-route-file inversion by repointing main.ts to conversation-forks. One seam per commit, safest first; after each seam typecheck + lint (incl. file-size guard) + FULL vitest suite must be green (TENET-10). Module-level singletons move atomically with their cluster. A no-loss audit test (added first) locks all 34 method+path registrations against silent loss. The PAN-2156 dependency gate is verified cleared (conversation-service.ts is now a 13-line barrel over services/conversation/*).
narratives.NonGoals:
- Do NOT barrel-split routes/conversations.ts into a sibling routes/conversations/ directory (the issue-body approach is superseded by Approach A).
- Do NOT rewrite handlers onto the Effect resolver/writer services or delete scattered read endpoints (PAN-1936 / PAN-2008 territory).
- Do NOT change any endpoint behavior, method, path, request/response shape, add or remove routes.
- Do NOT touch conversation-service.ts / services/conversation/* (PAN-2156's transcript-parsing domain).
- Do NOT grow src/lib/overdeck/conversations.ts past its 1526-line baseline; new logic goes to sibling door modules.
- Do NOT touch /ws/rpc, /ws/terminal, or EventRouter frontend flows.
- Do NOT add re-export shims in routes/conversations.ts; repoint importers instead.
- Do NOT introduce new explicit any; do NOT add execSync or sync tmux calls.

autoDecisions.summary: Approach A (two-door thinning) chosen over the issue-body barrel split.
autoDecisions.rationale: Operator confirmed the campaign-level ruling (docs/codebase-health/REFACTOR-QUEUE.md, 2026-07-02): route files are thinned behind src/lib/overdeck/ door modules, never barrel-split, because a route-file barrel split just relocates the god-file problem (workspaces barrel -> merge-ops.ts at 1925 lines). Matches the PAN-2148/PAN-2147 exemplars.

autoDecisions.summary: No-loss audit test authored FIRST (item item-noloss) before any extraction.
autoDecisions.rationale: The additive-refactor-no-loss rule requires an audit gate. Locking all 34 method+path registrations before moving anything means every subsequent seam is guarded against silently dropping a route; the test stays green throughout because routes never leave the file, only their bodies thin.

autoDecisions.summary: Seam order: diffs -> archive -> reads -> delivery -> runtime -> forks -> residue.
autoDecisions.rationale: Draft D5 'safest first': read-only self-contained diffs first, the stateful fork pipeline (touches the boot path) last but one, then a final residue-thinning + baseline-drop seam.

autoDecisions.summary: All seams are readiness=sequential, not parallel-dispatchable.
autoDecisions.rationale: Every seam edits the shared barrel routes/conversations.ts; concurrent seams would conflict on that file. This is a genuine shared-mutation ordering dependency, encoded as a blocks chain.

autoDecisions.summary: Two beads carry requiresInspection=true: the first extraction seam (diffs) and the fork seam.
autoDecisions.rationale: The first seam crystallizes the door-module + thin-adapter + repoint + baseline-update pattern every later seam copies; a wrong pattern cascades. The fork seam modifies the server boot path (main.ts) and carries the self.-spy subtlety. All other seams are mechanically caught by the full suite + file-size guard, so default to false.

autoDecisions.summary: Delivery seam may split into conversation-delivery.ts + conversation-message.ts.
autoDecisions.rationale: Draft D6: the delivery cluster (handleConversationMessage + transforms + control acks + delivery method) is the ceiling risk; if the single module would exceed 1000 lines, split message handling into a sibling. No new baseline entries either way.
